editions.label: 15 Oct
editions.title: Hotels take €508M, logistics +73%: Portugal's property capital rotates as volumes dip 13%
editions.summary: Portuguese commercial real estate drew €1.378 billion in H1 2026 — down 12.8% year-on-year, but a far milder slide than Europe's 23% drop. Hotels led the pack with €508M, up 25%, now 37% of all capital deployed. Industrial and logistics was the fastest-growing segment, up 73%. Retail fell roughly 30% as buyers turned selective. International investors still drive the market at around 55% of volume. Meanwhile Porto quietly hit a decade-high, and Lisbon put €60M of land on the block. Net: capital isn't leaving Portugal — it's moving to where occupancy and scarcity are, and away from where they aren't.
editions.hook: Portugal's property money is rotating — into hotels and sheds, out of shops.

items.headline: Boavista's Bessa stadium sells for €33M to the builders of Benfica's arena
items.summary: Frozenspark, part of the Confrasilvas group (the Maurício family behind Benfica's stadium), won creditor approval to buy the bankrupt club's Bessa stadium for €33M, just above the €32.92M floor. The site spans ~78,000 m² of built area plus a 21,000+ m² sports complex, with housing-and-commerce redevelopment flagged as possible.
items.why: A distressed sports asset with ~100,000 m² of central-Porto land, bought by an experienced stadium developer — a rare large-scale redevelopment play in a supply-starved city.

items.headline: Lisbon puts 10 municipal plots worth €60M up for public auction
items.summary: The city council will auction ten plots totalling ~30,000 m² on 10 December, with a combined base value near €60M — led by sites in Penha de França (€13.7M), Marvila (€11.9M) and Campolide (€10.9M). Proceeds fund the council's investment plan through 2030.
items.why: Rare prime development land coming to market in a city where buildable plots — not capital — are the scarce input, and a fresh price benchmark for developers.

items.headline: Hotels take €508M as commercial volumes dip 13% — and logistics jumps 73%
items.summary: Colliers' H1 2026 snapshot puts total commercial investment at €1.378bn, down 12.8% but well ahead of Europe's 23% fall. Hotels led at €508M (+25%, 37% of the market); industrial & logistics grew fastest at +73% to €169M; retail slipped ~30% to €422M. Foreign capital is ~55% of the total.
items.why: The capital map is rotating — underwrite hotels and logistics on occupancy and scarcity, and treat retail as an asset-level, not sector-level, bet.

items.headline: Greater Porto hits a decade-high €451M as office take-up jumps 37%
items.summary: Cushman & Wakefield's first Porto market report logs €451M of commercial investment in H1, up 8% and a ten-year record. Office take-up rose 37% through August with 90,000+ m² in the pipeline; retail openings climbed 50%; logistics demand outruns a shortage of modern space. Valongo, Trofa, Santo Tirso and Santa Maria da Feira are emerging as hubs.
items.why: Porto is outrunning the national trend — a decade-high for capital and the strongest office demand in years, concentrated in prime, sustainable stock.

items.headline: House prices rebound 3.4% to €3,666/m² — but Lisbon cools and sales drag
items.summary: Doutor Finanças' Observatório puts advertised prices up 3.4% in Q3 to a €3,666/m² national average, recovering from a Q2 dip. But Lisbon fell 1.4% (still €5,582/m²) while Viseu led at +12.5%, and the average apartment now takes 132 days to sell — up 25%. Rents were flat at €15.48/m², with Lisbon down 5.4%.
items.why: Prices still climb nationally while Lisbon cools and selling times stretch — the market is bifurcating by geography and price band, rewarding disciplined entry.

items.headline: Logistics pipeline tops 1.1M m² through 2029 as Portugal lands on the global radar
items.summary: B. Prime's Prime Mile report records ~199,000 m² of H1 industrial & logistics take-up and a 2026–2029 pipeline expected to exceed 1.1M m², with prime rents still rising. The drivers: e-commerce, the Port of Sines and Portos 5+ plan, rail upgrades, and data-centre demand.
items.why: A 1.1M m² pipeline signals logistics is institutionalising — yet a shortage of modern space keeps pushing prime rents up.

items.headline: Government targets a full inventory of all state-owned property by 2030
items.summary: The 2027 State Budget proposal (OE2027), now before Parliament, sets a 2030 deadline to catalogue every state-owned asset — including properties assigned to third parties and those still misregistered to private owners or extinct entities. The third phase runs 2027–2030 and feeds a full accounting inventory.
items.why: A complete state asset register is the precursor to disposals and public-private deals — a potentially large future pipeline of public land and buildings.

items.headline: Four Portuguese projects make the Dezeen Awards 2026 shortlist
items.summary: From 152 shortlisted projects across 36 countries: Casa Plaj by Extrastudio (House, rural), Mercado do Bairro Padre Cruz by REDO architects (Civic), the Canning Factory by OODA (Heritage), and Casa Sem Pele by Didier Faustino (Small Project). Winners are announced 16 November at London's Royal Opera House.
items.why: Heritage conversions and civic-market regeneration are exactly the adaptive-reuse plays drawing investor capital — and Portuguese studios are setting the template.

readForFund.text: Hotels (+25%) and logistics (+73%) are where occupancy and scarcity live; retail (−30%) needs asset-level conviction, not beta.
A decade-high €451M and +37% office take-up say the second city is no longer the discount play.
Lisbon's €60M auction and Boavista's ~100,000 m² prove buildable plots, not capital, are the scarce input.
A 2030 inventory of public property is the leading indicator of the next wave of disposals and PPP land.

editions.label: 14 Oct
editions.title: UBS puts Lisbon on its global property-bubble list for the first time
editions.summary: Lisbon has entered the UBS Global Real Estate Bubble Index for the first time, landing in elevated-risk territory. Real house prices have climbed about 7% a year over the past decade — the fastest of the 23 cities UBS tracks — and roughly 10% since mid-2025. The signal lands just as Budget 2027 doubles down on bricks: urban-rehab tax breaks are extended to 2031 and the IRS rent deduction rises to €1,000. Yet the heat is easing at the edges — asking rents have stabilised at +5.2% and buy-to-let yields slipped to 6.8% with lower risk. Capital keeps finding the deals, from the €33M Bessa stadium sale in Porto to €60M of Lisbon municipal assets heading to auction. Net: prices look stretched and policy still favours the builder — underwrite for a cooler 2027, not a replay of the last decade.
editions.hook: Lisbon just joined UBS's global property-bubble watchlist — a first.

items.headline: Boavista's Bessa stadium sells for €33M to Confrasilvas
items.summary: Frozenspark, part of the Maurício family's Confrasilvas group, won creditor approval to buy Boavista FC's Estádio do Bessa and sports complex for €33M, just above the €32.92M auction floor. The ~78,000 m² site — with 21,000+ m² of development potential — could host a mixed-use scheme of housing and retail.
items.why: A bankrupt club's trophy asset becomes a central-Porto land play — distressed sports and institutional property is where patient capital still finds scale inside the city.

items.headline: Lisbon council sends €60M of property to public auction
items.summary: Câmara de Lisboa will put ten municipal properties, valued together at about €60M, under the hammer on 10 December.
items.why: Rare direct access to prime municipal stock — a route into Lisbon assets outside the broker-led process, if reserve prices leave room to create value.

items.headline: Gaia riverfront scheme sells 94% before completion
items.summary: The Royal Pescaria project on Vila Nova de Gaia's historic waterfront is 94.4% sold ahead of delivery, with just one of its 18 apartments left.
items.why: Prime, small-lot riverfront product still clears off-plan — evidence that scarcity beats any broad market slowdown in the Porto/Gaia core.

items.headline: Budget 2027 earmarks €174M for Lisbon & Porto metro expansion
items.summary: The 2027 State Budget proposal allocates €174M to extend the Lisbon and Porto metro networks.
items.why: New stations reprice the land around them — the corridors on each extension are where early site assembly pays off well before the lines open.

items.headline: Matosinhos to host the first CICA architecture-criticism congress in Portugal
items.summary: Casa da Arquitetura in Matosinhos will stage the first International Committee of Architectural Critics (CICA) congress ever held in Portugal, convening critics largely in person.
items.why: Portugal's design reputation is a soft-power asset for developers — global critical attention lifts the premium on well-authored Portuguese schemes.

items.headline: Budget 2027: rehab tax breaks extended to 2031, rent deduction up to €1,000
items.summary: The OE2027 proposal prolongs urban-rehabilitation tax benefits for another five years, to 2031, and lifts the IRS deduction for tenants' rent by €100 to €1,000.
items.why: A five-year runway on rehab incentives underpins value-add underwriting — refurbishment keeps its fiscal edge over new-build well into the next cycle.

items.headline: Porto leans on owners of ~6,400 vacant buildings
items.summary: Porto's council has flagged about 6,400 potentially vacant buildings and signalled it may raise IMI on owners who fail to act.
items.why: Penal IMI turns dormant stock into either a cost or a forced sale — watch Porto's vacant registry for discounted acquisition targets.

items.headline: Asking rents cool, steadying at +5.2%
items.summary: After rising through the year, residential rents across Portugal are levelling off, with annual growth settling around 5.2%.
items.why: Rent growth decelerating toward mid-single digits caps income upside — the next leg of returns has to come from basis, not from runaway rents.

items.headline: Buy-to-let gross yield holds at 6.8% in Q3, with lower risk
items.summary: Gross residential rental yield came in at 6.8% in the third quarter — slightly below a year earlier — while the investment risk attached to it fell.
items.why: Yields compressing on lower risk is late-cycle behaviour — price discipline at entry matters more now than chasing headline cash-on-cash.

readForFund.text: UBS's bubble flag and stabilising rents say the easy price gains are behind us — model mid-single-digit growth, not the last decade's run.
Rehab tax breaks running to 2031 and sweeter rent deductions keep value-add and refurbishment fiscally ahead of new-build.
From the €33M Bessa stadium to €60M of Lisbon municipal lots, the cleanest access to scale runs through creditors and councils, not the open market.
Porto's move to penalise ~6,400 empty buildings via IMI should surface forced sellers — keep the acquisition list ready.

editions.label: 13 Oct
editions.title: Budget extends rehab tax breaks to 2031; high-speed rail breaks ground
editions.summary: The government's OE2027 proposal extends the IMI and IMT exemptions for urban rehabilitation to 2031 — a five-year runway for buildings over 30 years old inside ARUs that lift their condition by two grades. Tenants get a bigger break too: the IRS rent deduction rises to €1,000. On the ground, construction finally started on the Campanhã–Oiã leg of the Lisbon–Porto high-speed line, a ~€2bn Mota-Engil-led job with a new Santo Ovídio station in Gaia. Kronos Homes committed €125M+ to Distrikt, 214 homes in Parque das Nações. And Porto just posted its first annual rent fall since 2021, even as sale prices hit a record €4,346/m². Net: the policy window for value-add rehab stays open — but a two-speed market rewards discipline over momentum.
editions.hook: The 2027 Budget hands value-add a five-year runway.

items.headline: Confrasilvas buys Boavista's Bessa stadium for €33M
items.summary: Boavista's creditors approved the Maurício family's Confrasilvas (via Frozenspark) at €33M — just above the €32.92M auction floor — for the ~78,000 m² stadium plus a 21,000 m² sports complex. The club had debts above €150M.
items.why: Distressed sports real estate is becoming a land play — a central, well-connected Porto parcel with clear mixed-use (housing + commercial) upside at a discipline-tested price.

items.headline: Tomás Ribeiro 89 in Picoas changes hands, permits in place
items.summary: A 1920s heritage building in Avenidas Novas — six two-to-five-bed apartments by ARX Portugal, 20 parking spaces and an 895 m² garden — sold fully licensed and ready to build. Dils and CBRE advised; price undisclosed.
items.why: Shovel-ready, consented prime-Lisbon stock is what trades fastest right now — buyers are paying up to skip the permitting risk that stalls everyone else.

items.headline: Lisbon–Porto high-speed rail breaks ground
items.summary: Works began on the 71 km Campanhã–Oiã section — a ~€2bn concession led by Mota-Engil's AVAN Norte, backed by €875M EIB + €480M CEF2 — including a new Douro bridge and an underground Santo Ovídio station in Gaia. Full line targeted for 2032, with a 1h15 Lisbon–Porto trip.
items.why: New HSR stations re-rate land. Santo Ovídio's intermodal hub and Busquets masterplan make Gaia the clearest medium-term value corridor — assemble ahead of the 2032 clock.

items.headline: Kronos commits €125M+ to Distrikt in Parque das Nações
items.summary: Kronos Homes' largest scheme to date: four towers, 214 one-to-five-bed homes, six retail units and a public car park, designed by Morph Studio with floors rotated 45° for Tagus views. Group portfolio is ~18,000 homes, ~€500M revenue.
items.why: Institutional capital is still betting on prime Lisbon at scale — a signal that the top of the market, unlike the mid-tier, isn't waiting for rate relief.

items.headline: MVGM scales Iberian hotel management to 77 assets
items.summary: The manager added 47 hotel properties in 2026 to reach 77 under management across Spain and Portugal — 9,067 rooms and 553,000+ m² of urban and resort hotels plus tourist apartments.
items.why: Owners are outsourcing hospitality ops at speed — a tell that institutional hotel capital is consolidating in Iberia and prizing asset-management depth.

items.headline: Savills relocates its Porto office to VIVA Offices
items.summary: The agency is moving its Porto base into the VIVA Offices scheme, a bet on upgraded prime workspace in the city — and a vote of confidence in its own northern pipeline.
items.why: When the brokers themselves trade up to new-build offices, it flags where Porto's occupier demand — and prime rents — are heading.

items.headline: Segmento Urbano launches AI planning-compliance checks
items.summary: The firm rolled out an AI service that checks architectural projects against regulatory and urban-planning rules before submission — aimed at cutting the back-and-forth that delays câmara approvals.
items.why: Licensing lag is Portugal's biggest hidden cost. Tools that de-risk the permit timeline go straight to IRR — faster approvals, less dead capital.

items.headline: OE2027: rehab tax breaks extended to 2031, rent deduction up to €1,000
items.summary: The draft budget keeps the IMI exemption (3 years, 5 if let) and the IMT exemption for rehabilitated ARU buildings over 30 years old running to 2031. The IRS rent deduction rises €100 to €1,000 (€1,100 for the lowest bracket). Not yet law.
items.why: A five-year certain horizon lets value-add rehab underwrite the full IMI/IMT saving — it meaningfully improves the maths on older ARU stock. Watch the final vote.

items.headline: Lisbon's AL licences down 37% — but the homes aren't coming back
items.summary: Lisbon now has 11,704 local-accommodation licences, 37% fewer than 2025, yet few of those units have returned to the long-term residential market — undercutting the core premise of the AL clampdown.
items.why: Supply policy is missing its target. Expect renewed political pressure — and possibly blunter rules — which keeps AL-exposed assets a regulatory risk to price in.

items.headline: Porto: a market at two speeds — rents fall, prices hit records
items.summary: Porto city rents fell 4.4% year-on-year in September — the first drop since 2021 — to a median €19/m², while sale prices jumped 9% to a record €4,346/m². Matosinhos passed €3,500/m² and Gaia €3,000/m² for the first time. Construction costs are also up 7.5% year-on-year.
items.why: Rents cooling while capital values climb compresses yields — a warning for rental underwriting in Porto, and a reason to favour build-to-sell or value-add over hold-for-yield there.

readForFund.lead: The rehab window just got longer.
readForFund.text: If OE2027 passes, the IMI/IMT breaks on 30+ year ARU stock run to 2031 — underwrite the full saving on value-add deals, not a two-year sliver.

readForFund.lead: Buy the station, not the hype.
readForFund.text: HSR groundbreaking makes Gaia/Santo Ovídio the cleanest land-assembly story — but the 2032 clock means patience, not a quick flip.
Falling rents against record prices compress going-in yields — tilt north toward build-to-sell and consented value-add, away from hold-for-income.
From Tomás Ribeiro 89 to the AL misfire, the premium is on permit certainty — shovel-ready assets and tools that compress licensing time are where the alpha sits.

editions.label: 12 Oct
editions.title: Draycott buys ECS from Davidson Kempner, building a €3bn+ Portuguese property platform
editions.summary: Draycott, the alternative-asset house led by João Coelho Borges, has agreed to buy ECS — one of Portugal's largest managers of tourism and real-estate assets — from US fund Davidson Kempner. The deal lands months after Draycott absorbed Square AM, pushing its platform past €3 billion in assets. Davidson Kempner paid about €850 million for ECS at the end of 2022 and has since sold pieces, including the Conrad Algarve for €150 million; it stays on as a strategic partner. Terms were not disclosed, and the deal has been notified to the Autoridade da Concorrência. Meanwhile, the OE2027 budget would cut VAT on construction from 23% to 6% while build costs climbed 7.5% year on year in August. Net: capital is concentrating in fewer, bigger Portuguese platforms just as building gets more expensive and the State leans on tax to unblock supply.
editions.hook: Draycott is buying ECS — and consolidating Portuguese property fast

items.headline: Draycott agrees to buy ECS from Davidson Kempner
items.summary: Draycott — João Coelho Borges's alternative-asset manager, already past €3bn after swallowing Square AM — will acquire ECS, the tourism-and-real-estate house Davidson Kempner bought for ~€850M in 2022. Terms undisclosed; the deal is before the competition authority.
items.why: A second major independent manager folding into Draycott in a year reshapes the buy-side — fewer, larger platforms sit on the other side of every Portuguese deal you do.

items.headline: Santarém gets a premium Tagus-view scheme, Andaluz Residence
items.summary: The Andaluz Residence is under construction on Avenida Madre Andaluz in Santarém's upscale quarter, positioned as a premium concept overlooking the Tejo.
items.why: Upper-tier product is spreading to secondary riverside cities — a read on where developers see pricing power beyond the metros.

items.headline: New 47-home scheme IRIS Açoteia rises in Olhão
items.summary: IRIS Açoteia brings 47 apartments in T1–T3 layouts to Olhão, set between the Ria Formosa lagoon and the town centre.
items.why: The eastern Algarve keeps drawing mid-density residential — steady absorption outside the saturated Golden Triangle.

items.headline: OE2027 earmarks €174M for Lisbon and Porto metro expansion
items.summary: The draft 2027 budget allocates about €174 million to extending the Lisbon and Porto metro networks.
items.why: New stations redraw catchment areas — transit lines are among the most reliable signals for where land and rents re-rate.

items.headline: Carvalho Araújo demands answers on 204 promised homes
items.summary: Atelier Carvalho Araújo says it is still waiting — three years after winning the design competition — for the contract to develop a 204-home affordable project in Matosinhos.
items.why: A public reminder of how slowly State-led affordable pipelines convert from competition to contract — execution risk on the supply the market is counting on.

items.headline: Matosinhos to host architecture criticism's CICA congress
items.summary: Casa da Arquitetura in Matosinhos will stage the first CICA (international architecture critics) conference held in Portugal, largely back in person.
items.why: More global design attention on Portugal burnishes the build-quality story that underpins premium pricing and the export of Portuguese studios.

items.headline: Focus Group to design a €25M office tower in Algeria
items.summary: Portuguese firm Focus Group will design a new office tower for Algerian personal-care company Faderco, deepening its North African footprint.
items.why: Portuguese architecture and engineering practices are increasingly exporting billings — a diversification worth tracking as domestic margins tighten.

items.headline: OE2027 cuts construction VAT to 6%, carves out rental reform
items.summary: The 2027 budget proposal drops VAT on construction from 23% to 6% (~€94M cost), adds IRS relief for landlords charging up to €2,300, and keeps IMT/IS exemptions for under-35 first buyers — but the rental-law revision is pulled out for separate talks. Debate 27–28 Oct; final vote 24 Nov.
items.why: The VAT cut materially improves new-build economics, but with rental reform parked, the income side of the investment case stays unresolved.

items.headline: New-home build costs up 7.5% year on year in August
items.summary: INE's construction-cost index rose 7.5% YoY in August (labour +8.0%, materials +7.1%), with diesel and copper up ~30%; prices have climbed sharply since March on higher energy costs.
items.why: Cost inflation is re-accelerating just as the VAT cut arrives — underwrite build budgets on the current curve, not last year's.

readForFund.text: Two big independents (Square AM, now ECS) folding into Draycott in one year means fewer counterparties and more scale across the table on any deal.
A 7.5% annual build-cost rise — diesel and copper up ~30% — eats margin on anything priced today; stress new-build budgets hard.

readForFund.lead: The tax tailwind is real but narrow.
readForFund.text: VAT at 6% on construction and landlord IRS relief help delivery economics, but rental-law reform was pulled from the budget, so the income side stays uncertain.
Santarém, Olhão and Torres Vedras all saw new upper-tier residential this week — pricing power is spreading beyond the Lisbon / Porto / Algarve cores.

editions.label: 11 Oct
editions.title: Draycott to buy ECS from Davidson Kempner, consolidating Portugal's RE fund management
editions.summary: US fund Davidson Kempner has agreed to sell ECS — one of Portugal's largest alternative-asset managers, built on post-crisis tourism and real estate pulled off bank balance sheets — to Draycott, already steward of over €3bn and fresh from buying Square Asset Management. Davidson Kempner paid roughly €850m for ECS in 2022 and stays on as a strategic partner; the deal is now before Portugal's competition authority. The backdrop is a budget week that matters more than the headline deal: OE2027 earmarks €2.003bn for affordable housing, cuts construction VAT to 6%, keeps first-home IMT/IS exemptions, and softens IRS on moderate rents. Sonae Sierra named a new CEO, and the Oeste and Santarém pipelines added premium stock. Net: ownership of Portugal's fund-management shelf is consolidating into fewer, bigger hands — just as the state writes a €2bn supply cheque.
editions.hook: Draycott is quietly rolling up Portugal's real estate fund managers.

items.headline: Davidson Kempner sells manager ECS to Draycott
items.summary: Draycott — €3bn+ in alternatives and recent buyer of Square Asset Management — is acquiring ECS, the platform Davidson Kempner bought for ~€850m in 2022 and whose assets have included the Conrad Algarve. Terms undisclosed; notified to the Autoridade da Concorrência.
items.why: Portugal's independent fund-management universe is being rolled up into a handful of large sponsors — reshaping who you co-invest alongside and who sets pricing on tourism and NPL-sourced portfolios.

items.headline: State targets €530m from selling public property in 2027
items.summary: The 2027 budget pencils in ~€530.3m of disposals — €324.8m in buildings and €178.3m in housing — and the state plans to inventory its entire property estate by 2030.
items.why: A half-billion-euro public pipeline plus a full asset inventory is a multi-year source of off-market stock — land and buildings that rarely reach open-market agents.

items.headline: Six contemporary villas rise among the Oeste vineyards
items.summary: Quinta de Santo António in Turcifal (Torres Vedras) will deliver six T4+1 villas over 2+1 levels, pitched as a design-led rural retreat within easy reach of Lisbon.
items.why: Low-density, high-spec schemes in the Oeste are testing whether buyers will pay Lisbon-adjacent premiums an hour outside the city — a live question for land plays beyond the capital.

items.headline: Santarém gets a premium project with Tejo views
items.summary: The Andaluz Residence is under construction on Avenida Madre Andaluz, bringing a premium housing concept to a secondary market more associated with value than luxury.
items.why: Premium product is migrating into interior cities like Santarém — a signal of where developers see headroom now that Lisbon and Porto pricing has stalled.

items.headline: €174m for Lisbon and Porto metro expansion in OE2027
items.summary: The 2027 budget allocates €174m to extend both metro networks — continued public investment in the transit corridors that underpin urban land values.
items.why: New stations reprice the land around them. Tracking confirmed alignments is one of the cleaner ways to front-run value uplift in both cities.

items.headline: Luís Mota Duarte to lead Sonae Sierra from 2027
items.summary: Sonae Sierra named Luís Mota Duarte as next CEO from January 2027, succeeding Fernando Guedes de Oliveira after more than 15 years at the helm of the retail-and-development group.
items.why: A generational change at one of Iberia's biggest retail-RE platforms can shift its appetite for development, disposals and third-party mandates — worth watching for anyone in its orbit.

items.headline: Savills opens a custom Porto office at VIVA Offices
items.summary: The adviser's Porto team has moved into a purpose-fitted space at VIVA Offices, deepening the big-brand brokerage footprint in the northern market.
items.why: International advisers committing fitted space to Porto is a vote of confidence in deal flow outside Lisbon — and more competition for local agents.

items.headline: Focus Group takes Portuguese design to a €25m Algerian tower
items.summary: Portuguese firm Focus Group is designing a €25m office tower for Algerian company Faderco, extending its presence in North Africa.
items.why: Portugal's design and engineering studios are increasingly export businesses — a reminder that the country's built-environment talent is a tradeable asset, not just a domestic one.

items.headline: OE2027: VAT on construction cut to 6%, first-home exemptions stay
items.summary: The 2027 budget cuts construction VAT from 23% to 6% (~€94m cost), keeps IMT/IS exemptions for first owner-occupied homes, and lowers IRS on "moderate" rents up to €2,300 (~€209m cost). Rental-law changes are being negotiated separately. General debate 27–28 Oct; final vote 24 Nov.
items.why: A 17-point VAT cut on construction is a direct margin lever for developers — and the moderate-rent IRS break nudges the economics of build-to-rent.

items.headline: First White Paper on short-term lets, led by Caldeira Cabral
items.summary: Former economy minister Manuel Caldeira Cabral will coordinate Portugal's first White Paper on alojamento local, due by May 2027 — the groundwork for the next round of AL rules.
items.why: AL regulation has whipsawed valuations for years. A formal evidence base signals the policy direction — and the timeline — for anyone underwriting short-let yield.

items.headline: Dwelling Portugal: 210 deals, €50m+ in year one
items.summary: The 100% Portuguese-owned brokerage — backed by ex-athletes and fintech Doutor Finanças — closed 210 deals at an average above €368,000 across Lisbon, Cascais, Porto and the Algarve, in what it calls a more selective, deliberate market.
items.why: A €368k average and "more demanding buyers" confirm the market has shifted from momentum to selection — underwriting, not discovery, is where returns are now made.

readForFund.text: As Draycott absorbs ECS and Square, fewer, larger sponsors will set pricing on tourism and NPL-sourced portfolios — know who you're bidding against.

readForFund.lead: The state is both buyer-side and supplier.
readForFund.text: A €2bn affordable-housing cheque and a €530m disposal pipeline make the public sector the biggest single mover in the market next year.

readForFund.lead: The VAT cut is a margin gift.
readForFund.text: 23% to 6% on construction reshapes feasibility — marginal schemes pencil, and build-to-rent gains from the moderate-rent IRS break.
Santarém and the Oeste are the frontier for high-spec product — the land math there, not in stalled Lisbon, is where the next spread sits.

editions.label: 10 Oct
editions.title: OE2027 puts €2bn behind housing — and lifts the IMT Jovem ceiling to €338k
editions.summary: The Government's OE2027 proposal, delivered to Parliament on Wednesday night, earmarks €2,003 million to expand affordable housing and rebuild the public stock. The bulk — €1,071M — goes to the IHRU for new supply and rehabilitation, with €917M for rental support (Porta 65+, PAER, affordable-rent tax breaks) and €15M to digitise urban licensing. The budget also moves to finance 45,000 homes dropped from the PRR and leans on public-private partnerships built on State-owned land. On the demand side, the IMT Jovem exemption for under-35 first-time buyers rises to €338,141 and all IMT brackets step up 2.3%. The parliamentary debate runs 27–28 October, with the final global vote set for 24 November. Net: supply is the stated priority, but the money that actually moves deals is still the IMT relief and the land the State is willing to let go.
editions.hook: Portugal's 2027 budget bets €2bn on housing supply

items.headline: Lisbon council lists 10 properties for auction, targeting €60M
items.summary: The Câmara de Lisboa is putting ten sites — nearly 30,000 m² across the city — to public auction on 10 December, with base bids from €1.1M to €13.7M (the largest a 10,000 m² plot in Penha de França). Proceeds fund the council's investment plan to 2030; the land is explicitly not earmarked for housing.
items.why: A rare block of developable inner-city land coming to market at once — and a read on where the municipality itself values plots across Penha de França, Marvila, Campolide and Beato.

items.headline: MVGM adds 47 hotels, reaching 77 assets under management
items.summary: Property manager MVGM has grown its Iberian hotel book by 47 assets to 77 under management, consolidating its position in the segment that is drawing the most capital.
items.why: Operating platforms, not just owners, are scaling fastest in hospitality — mandates flow to whoever can run the assets, which is how institutional capital enters the trade.

items.headline: Kronos Homes commits €125M+ to 214-home Distrikt in Parque das Nações
items.summary: Kronos Homes is investing over €125M in Distrikt, its largest residential scheme to date: 214 homes (T1–T5) across four towers, plus six retail units and a public car park in Lisbon's Parque das Nações, designed by Morph Studio. The project won Best Real Estate Project at the 2026 World Class District Awards in Madrid.
items.why: A top-tier institutional developer doubling down on prime Lisbon residential signals continued conviction in the high-end band even as affordability dominates the policy conversation.

items.headline: IHRU to build 204 affordable homes in Matosinhos — now on EIB money
items.summary: With the project (est. €35.2M) dropped from the PRR, the IHRU says it will fund 204 affordable-rent homes at Parque de Picoutos via its EIB facility — which backs up to 12,000 affordable homes by 2030. Atelier Carvalho Araújo was picked in 2023, but says it still has no signed contract.
items.why: The template for Portugal's post-PRR affordable pipeline: EIB debt replacing grant money, with the execution risk that tenders stalled for years still carry.

items.headline: Savills opens a bespoke Porto office at VIVA Offices
items.summary: Savills Portugal's Porto team has moved into VIVA Offices in Ramalde — a 21,500 m², nine-floor building owned by Sonae Sierra and GFH, designed by Broadway Malyan and in line for LEED Platinum. MD Ricardo Valente frames it as a commitment to the North.
items.why: The international agencies are staffing up around Porto, confirming the North as the next institutional battleground beyond Lisbon — and that modern, certified office stock still lets space there.

items.headline: Four Portuguese projects make the Dezeen Awards 2026 shortlist
items.summary: Portugal lands four of the 152 shortlisted projects: Casa Plaj by Extrastudio (Lourinhã), Mercado do Bairro Padre Cruz by REDO architects (Lisbon), the Canning Factory conversion by OODA (Matosinhos), and Casa Sem Pele by Didier Faustino (Ribatejo). Winners are announced 16 November in London.
items.why: Heritage conversion (OODA's cannery) and civic regeneration are where Portuguese studios are winning global recognition — the asset classes where design quality most directly drives value.

items.headline: OE2027 injects €2,003M to reinforce housing supply in 2027
items.summary: The 2027 Budget commits €2,003M to affordable housing: €1,071M to the IHRU for new supply and rehabilitation, €917M for rental support, and €15M to digitise licensing. It also pledges to finance 45,000 homes cut from the PRR and to open State land to public-private partnerships.
items.why: The clearest statement yet of where public capital is going — and the partnership-on-State-land model is the single biggest potential source of development-ready sites for private players.

items.headline: IMT Jovem exemption rises to €338k; all brackets up 2.3%
items.summary: OE2027 lifts the under-35 first-home exemption from IMT and Stamp Duty to €338,141, and raises every IMT bracket 2.3%: the permanent-home exemption threshold goes to €108,792 and the top 7.5% rate now starts above €1,177,323.
items.why: A higher youth ceiling pulls more transactions into the tax-free band — concentrating demand (and price pressure) just under €338k, exactly where volume developers should be building.

items.headline: Commercial investment hits €1.39bn in H1, up 13% — hotels and retail lead
items.summary: B. Prime's Prime Watch puts H1 2026 commercial investment at ~€1,386M, +13% y/y, with hotels and retail together taking 63% of capital. Lisbon office take-up reached 66,906 m² and logistics absorption 199,182 m²; data centres are now ~9% of the development pipeline, and yields are described as stable.
items.why: The capital map for the year: operational, income-producing assets (hotels, retail) are winning, while a thin office pipeline to 2028 flags a future supply squeeze in prime Lisbon.

items.headline: A quieter shift: Portugal's brokerage sector is heading for consolidation
items.summary: Licensed brokerages jumped from 7,270 (2020) to 11,174 (2025), per IMPIC — but with a structural shortage of homes to sell, transaction volumes can fall even as prices hold. The piece argues the market is tilting toward concentration, rewarding firms that generate their own deal flow.
items.why: Fewer transactions per firm means fee compression and churn ahead — a reason for capital to own origination rather than rent it from a crowded intermediary layer.

readForFund.text: Both the budget's PPP-on-State-land push and Lisbon's €60M auction point the same way — the pipeline that matters now is public land coming to market, not new private listings.
A €338k IMT Jovem ceiling widens the tax-free band for sub-35 buyers; underwrite exit demand around that threshold, not above it.
Hotels and retail took 63% of H1's €1.39bn and MVGM is scaling to 77 hotels — platforms that can run assets capture the capital that discovery alone cannot.
With 11,174 brokerages chasing a shrinking transaction pool, fee compression is coming — a reason to own deal flow rather than rent it.

editions.label: 09 Oct
editions.title: Draycott buys ECS from Davidson Kempner, forging a €3.5bn+ Portuguese alternatives platform
editions.summary: Draycott is buying ECS from New York's Davidson Kempner, folding a tourism-heavy property book into a Portuguese platform that already runs over €3.5bn. Davidson Kempner, which paid about €850m for ECS at the end of 2022, stays on as a strategic partner; the deal still needs Competition Authority and CMVM sign-off. The backdrop is a market that keeps drawing capital: JLL now counts Portugal as 23% of Southern Europe's real-estate debt this year, with non-bank lenders funding roughly 74% of deals. Greater Porto just logged a €451m investment record for the half — its best in a decade. And the new RJUE licensing regime is live, shifting planning risk onto developers. Net: capital is consolidating and financing is widening, but the people underwriting Portuguese real estate are changing.
editions.hook: Portugal's fund-management map just got redrawn.

items.headline: Draycott buys ECS from Davidson Kempner
items.summary: Draycott — the PE firm founded in 2019 by João Coelho Borges, with €3.5bn+ under management after absorbing Square AM — is acquiring ECS, the manager of a tourism-heavy book of hotels, resorts and golf built from post-crisis bank portfolios. Davidson Kempner, which bought ECS for ~€850m in 2022, remains a strategic partner; the deal awaits regulatory approval.
items.why: An independent Portuguese alternatives platform of this scale means the biggest, most complex national tickets will increasingly route through fewer, better-capitalised hands.

items.headline: Prime logistics box hits the market by Porto airport
items.summary: CBRE has an exclusive mandate on a 5,485 m² stand-alone warehouse-and-office unit in Vila Nova da Telha (Maia), 500m from the airport's cargo terminal, with 21 docks, 8m clear height and A28/A41/A4 access. It is pitched at occupiers expanding in the north.
items.why: Modern logistics space in Greater Porto is scarce, and scarcity near the airport is where rental growth is concentrating — a signal for yield-seeking developers.

items.headline: PortoBay Falésia closes for a €20M overhaul
items.summary: The Algarve hotel has shut its doors and is auctioning its furnishings online ahead of a ~€20m renovation, set to reopen under an adults-only concept. It is part of PortoBay's wider reinvestment across Madeira and the Algarve.
items.why: Repositioning rather than new-build is where Algarve hospitality value is being created — branded operators are trading up existing stock to defend record room rates.

items.headline: Luís Mota Duarte to lead Sonae Sierra from 2027
items.summary: The group's investment-management chief will take over as CEO in January 2027, succeeding Fernando Guedes de Oliveira after 15+ years. Mota Duarte joined Sonae in 2014 to run M&A and moved to Sierra — owner of Centro Colombo and NorteShopping — in 2018.
items.why: A dealmaker takes the helm of Portugal's largest retail landlord — a signal of more active capital recycling across its shopping-centre portfolio.

items.headline: New RJUE licensing regime is now in force
items.summary: In effect since 1 October, the revised urban-planning code replaces upfront municipal review with "prior communication" — works can start on the applicant's responsibility, with councils reviewing once, afterwards. Sale contracts must now state whether a property holds an urban-planning title.
items.why: Faster starts, but compliance liability shifts squarely onto developers, designers and site managers — and banks' stance on utilisation licences for mortgages is still unsettled.

items.headline: Porto overtakes Lisbon on new short-term lets
items.summary: Porto has registered more new Alojamento Local units than Lisbon in 2026 — a shift in where short-term-rental supply is growing as the capital's contention zones bite and the north draws more tourism capital.
items.why: AL licensing is the single biggest swing factor on short-stay yields — and the growth is now in the north, not Lisbon.

items.headline: Portugal is now 23% of Southern Europe's property debt
items.summary: JLL counts ~€560m of Portuguese real-estate financing to end-September — 23% of a €2.46bn Southern-European total across 21 deals. Non-bank lenders (debt funds, i-banks, insurers) now supply ~74% of volume; hospitality (42%) and logistics (26%) lead demand.
items.why: The lender pool is deeper than the banks alone — but JLL calls it "more selective," so asset quality and cash-flow visibility decide who gets funded.

items.headline: Greater Porto hits a €451M investment record
items.summary: Cushman & Wakefield's first Market Focus Porto puts H1 commercial investment at €451m, up 8% and the best in a decade, led by retail and hotels. Office take-up rose 37% through August, with 90,000+ m² of modern space under development.
items.why: Porto has graduated from secondary market to a core allocation — and a thin modern pipeline keeps rental tension on the developers' side.

items.headline: H1 investment hits €1.39bn as data centres emerge
items.summary: B. Prime's Prime Watch puts national H1 commercial investment at €1,386m, up 13%, with hotels and retail at 63% of capital. Lisbon absorbed 66,906 m² of offices and 199,182 m² of logistics — data centres are now ~9% of space under development.
items.why: The fundamentals are solid, but B. Prime warns the office pipeline to 2028 may undershoot demand — and data centres are the new competitor for industrial land.

readForFund.text: The ECS deal builds a €3.5bn+ independent platform — the biggest Portuguese tickets will route through fewer, deeper-pocketed managers.
With debt funds, i-banks and insurers at ~74% of financing, well-structured deals have more lenders to court — on stricter cash-flow terms.
Prior communication replaces upfront review, so compliance and liability now sit with promoters and designers — price the risk in.
A €451m regional record, faster rent growth and more new AL registrations make Greater Porto the momentum market.

editions.label: 8 Oct
editions.title: Davidson Kempner sells ECS, Portugal's biggest alt-asset manager, to Draycott
editions.summary: US fund Davidson Kempner has agreed to sell ECS — the Portuguese manager it bought for about €850m in 2022 — to Draycott, the alternatives house run by João Coelho Borges. ECS was built on tourism and real-estate assets carved out of Portuguese banks' post-crisis balance sheets. Draycott already runs more than €3bn and recently absorbed Square Asset Management, making it one of the dominant local platforms. Terms were undisclosed and the deal still needs Autoridade da Concorrência clearance. Elsewhere today: Sonae Sierra lined up a new CEO, the government split its rental-law reform from the 2027 budget, and asking rents accelerated again. Net: consolidation among Portugal's alternative managers is speeding up — scale and bank relationships are becoming the moat.
editions.hook: Portugal's biggest alternatives manager is changing hands.

items.headline: Davidson Kempner sells ECS to Draycott
items.summary: The US fund is offloading ECS — one of Portugal's largest alternative and private-asset managers, built from distressed bank portfolios — to João Coelho Borges's Draycott, which already oversees €3bn+. Terms undisclosed; Davidson Kempner stays on as a strategic partner.
items.why: A landmark consolidation — the platforms that cleaned up Portugal's post-crisis NPLs are now the targets. Scale and workout expertise are what's being bought.

items.headline: Former Levira furniture factory heads to auction at €9.98m
items.summary: The ex-Levira industrial complex in Oiã (Aveiro) is up for online auction with a €9.98m opening bid, with bidding open until 9 October.
items.why: A rare large industrial-repositioning play in the Aveiro corridor — and a live read on where reserve pricing sits for secondary industrial land.

items.headline: State transfers 25.6ha Bobadela site to Loures
items.summary: Loures takes ~256,000 m² of the former Bobadela rail-logistics complex — now Parque Papa Francisco — for €196,400, with €9.45m of infrastructure investment committed through 2030 and the riverside zone earmarked for green and public space.
items.why: Public land being requalified on Lisbon's eastern edge reshapes the Loures regeneration pipeline — and the value of land around it.

items.headline: Matosinhos to build 108 homes on the old Leixões ground
items.summary: The câmara plans 108 dwellings, shops, an underground car park and a public square on the club's former pitch — an urban-infill redevelopment in Greater Porto.
items.why: Municipal-led infill on legacy sites is where new urban supply is actually coming from — watch the delivery model (public, private or JV).

items.headline: Seven Algarve councils bid €105m+ for social housing
items.summary: Seven Algarve municipalities filed 11 Algarve2030 applications for social housing, a programme worth more than €105m.
items.why: EU-funded public housing is a counter-cyclical source of construction demand in a region otherwise driven by tourism and second homes.

items.headline: Luís Mota Duarte named Sonae Sierra CEO from January 2027
items.summary: The investment-management chief succeeds Fernando Guedes de Oliveira, CEO for 15+ years. Sonae Sierra closed 2025 at 98% occupancy and in 2026 formed a ~€1.5bn JV with Norges Bank to buy eight Spanish shopping centres.
items.why: A generational handover at Iberia's biggest retail landlord — and a signal that shopping-centre capital is back on offense.

items.headline: Coldwell Banker opens first Porto office, absorbs Homelovers team
items.summary: Marking its 120th anniversary, the brand opens its first Porto agency and folds in a 10-person team from Homelovers Porto.
items.why: International-brand expansion into Porto signals where brokers expect transaction volume to grow next.

items.headline: Montenegro splits the rental-law reform from the 2027 budget
items.summary: The PM pulled rental-law negotiations out of OE2027 talks. The AD reform — faster evictions, more contract flexibility and scrapping the 2% cap on new-contract increases — cleared its first vote on 30 Sept after Chega abstained, and is now in committee.
items.why: A more landlord-friendly regime would reprice rental underwriting — but the path still depends on Chega/PS, so model both outcomes.

items.headline: Existing-contract rents can rise 2.56% in 2027
items.summary: The official update coefficient for ongoing leases is set at 2.56% for 2027, up from 2.24% in 2026, based on final inflation.
items.why: This is the cap on in-place rent growth for existing contracts — it directly sets NOI growth on stabilised residential.

items.headline: Asking rents accelerate to +6.1% year-on-year in September
items.summary: idealista's index shows asking rents up 6.1% year-on-year in September — a third straight month of acceleration — while 7% of luxury listings cut prices in Q2, the most since early 2025.
items.why: Market asking rents still outrun the 2.56% coefficient on in-place leases — the widening gap is the core thesis for rental-exposed strategies.

readForFund.text: The ECS sale shows scale and bank-workout relationships — not origination — command the premium among Portugal's alternative managers.
Bobadela, the old Leixões ground and €105m of Algarve social housing — municipal and EU-funded sites are where new supply is actually originating.

readForFund.lead: Underwrite the rent gap, not the headline.
readForFund.text: Market rents (+6.1%) keep outrunning the 2.56% cap on in-place leases; the spread is the return, and the reform could widen it.
A landlord-friendly rental law is live but hostage to Chega/PS — size positions to both the capped and uncapped case.

editions.label: 7 Oct
editions.title: Draycott buys ECS from Davidson Kempner, absorbing Portugal's post-crisis property platform
editions.summary: Draycott has agreed to buy ECS from Davidson Kempner, taking over one of Portugal's largest managers of post-crisis tourism and real-estate assets. Davidson Kempner paid roughly €850 million for ECS in late 2022 and has since sold assets such as the Conrad Algarve for €150 million. The buyer — led by João Coelho Borges and already running over €3 billion after absorbing Square Asset Management — stays focused on Portuguese property, tourism and private credit. Terms are undisclosed and the deal now sits with the Competition Authority. It lands as B. Prime pegs H1 commercial investment at €1.386 billion, up 13%, with hotels and retail taking 63% of capital. Net: ownership of Portugal's deepest distressed-property pool is consolidating into a single Lisbon-based alternatives house.
editions.hook: Portugal's biggest post-crisis property platform just changed hands.

items.headline: Draycott buys ECS from Davidson Kempner
items.summary: Davidson Kempner has agreed to sell ECS — one of Portugal's largest alternative-asset managers, built from post-crisis tourism and real-estate loans — to Draycott, which already runs over €3bn after buying Square Asset Management. Terms undisclosed; deal awaits regulatory clearance.
items.why: A single Lisbon alternatives house is consolidating control of Portugal's deepest pool of distressed tourism and property assets — reshaping who you transact with on big-ticket deals.

items.headline: Tomás Ribeiro 89 brings six apartments and an 895 m² garden to central Lisbon
items.summary: A 1920s building in Lisbon's Picoas district is being rehabilitated into six T2–T5 apartments wrapped around an 895 m² garden — a rare amount of private green space for the city centre.
items.why: Rehab-led, low-density luxury on scarce central plots stays the defensible play while new-build supply is tight and prices hold near record highs.

items.headline: Belas Clube de Campo's Native Townhouses enter final sales phase
items.summary: The T4 townhouses — 242 m² each on plots of 526–661 m² inside the Belas Clube de Campo resort near Sintra — are nearing sell-out.
items.why: Resort-style, low-density family housing on the Lisbon fringe keeps absorbing demand priced out of the core; a near sell-out signals continued depth in the €1m+ suburban segment.

items.headline: Bain opens a 2,000 m² Lisbon HQ in a Souto de Moura–restored 1875 palace
items.summary: Bain & Company has inaugurated its Lisbon headquarters across four floors (c. 2,000 m², up to 250 staff) in the Anjos Urban Palace at Príncipe Real — an 1875 mansion restored by Pritzker laureate Eduardo Souto de Moura, whose rehab won the UIA Gold Medal.
items.why: Blue-chip occupiers are still paying up for best-in-class, design-led heritage space in prime Lisbon — exactly the office product the market is short of.

items.headline: Atelier Carvalho Araújo presses the state over 204 promised homes
items.summary: Three years after winning the competition for a 204-unit affordable-housing scheme in Matosinhos, the studio is publicly demanding answers on why the project has stalled.
items.why: Public affordable-housing delivery keeps slipping from competition to construction — a reminder that policy ambition is outrunning execution, and private supply still carries the market.

items.headline: 2027 rent cap set at 2.56% as landlords await official publication
items.summary: On INE's final inflation data, existing-contract rents can rise up to 2.56% in 2027 — above 2026's 2.24% — once the coefficient is published in the Diário da República, expected late October, with a 30-day notice period.
items.why: The annual cap is the single biggest lever on in-place residential income; 2.56% barely tracks inflation, keeping real rental yields under pressure on regulated stock.

items.headline: Missing portaria leaves the new affordable-rental regime unusable
items.summary: An industry association warns the new affordable-rental scheme still can't be applied because the implementing regulation (portaria) hasn't been issued — stranding owners, investors and municipalities ready to use it.
items.why: Incentive regimes that exist on paper but not in practice are a recurring Portuguese risk; underwrite affordable-rental upside only once the enabling rules actually land.

items.headline: Commercial investment hits €1.39bn in H1, up 13%, led by hotels and retail
items.summary: B. Prime's Prime Watch puts H1 2026 commercial investment at €1.386bn (+13% y/y), with hotels and retail together taking 63% of capital; Lisbon absorbed c. 67,000 m² of offices and logistics c. 199,000 m², with data centres now ~9% of the pipeline.
items.why: The recovery is broadening beyond trophy offices into hospitality, logistics and data centres — where demand and yields still favour fresh capital.

items.headline: Global construction growth slows to 1.4% as costs and labour bite
items.summary: Worldwide construction is projected to grow just 1.4% in 2026, squeezed by energy and material costs, high interest rates and a shortage of skilled labour.
items.why: Flat output plus persistent cost inflation keeps the pipeline thin — supportive for values on existing, well-located stock but punishing for ground-up margins.

readForFund.text: With ECS folding into Draycott, Portugal's distressed-property and tourism platforms are concentrating into fewer, larger alternatives managers — fewer counterparties, bigger tickets.
Thin construction (1.4% global growth) and stalled public housing keep well-located existing stock scarce, underpinning values even as the cycle matures.
Hotels, retail, logistics and data centres — not just offices — are driving the 13% rise in commercial investment; breadth is where the next yield sits.

readForFund.lead: Watch the rulebook, not the rhetoric.
readForFund.text: A 2.56% rent cap and an affordable-rental regime still missing its portaria show regulated income and policy upside both hinge on paperwork that lags the market.

editions.label: 6 Oct
editions.title: Portugal leads EU house-price growth at 16.5% as asking prices hit €3,228/m² record
editions.summary: Portugal led the entire EU for house-price growth in Q2, up 16.5% year-on-year against a eurozone average of just 1.1%. The heat carried into autumn: September asking prices rose 7.9% to a record €3,228/m², even as quarterly growth cooled to +0.5%. It is happening while Euribor climbs and mortgage rates touch 3%, squeezing buyers but not supply-starved pricing. On the supply side, the new RJUE planning regime took effect on 1 October, promising faster licensing for construction, rehabilitation and sales. Capital keeps arriving — commercial investment hit €1.4bn in the first half — and the dealmaking rolled on this week, from Saldanha offices to Matosinhos redevelopment. Net: demand still vastly outruns supply, and the new rules are a bet that Portugal can finally build toward balance.
editions.hook: Portugal is the EU's hottest housing market — and prices just set another record.

items.headline: Arrow Global takes 6,200 m² for its new Lisbon home near Saldanha
items.summary: The credit and asset manager will occupy the whole of the República 5 building by Praça do Saldanha, a single-tenant base for roughly 700 staff.
items.why: A full-building letting to an institutional occupier shows prime Lisbon offices still draw demand even with rates rising — a bid under core office values.

items.headline: Former Levira furniture plant heads to auction at almost €10m
items.summary: Levira's old industrial complex in Oliveira do Bairro is listed with a €9.98m base price; bidding closes on 9 October.
items.why: Large industrial sites coming to market at a clearing price are exactly the value-add and logistics-conversion stock supply-starved funds are hunting.

items.headline: Matosinhos plans 108 homes and shops on the old Leixões ground
items.summary: The council wants 108 dwellings, ground-floor retail, underground parking and a public plaza on the former Leixões Sport Club pitch.
items.why: Municipal-led redevelopment of legacy sites is becoming a core pipeline source in Greater Porto — watch it for JV and forward-purchase entry points.

items.headline: State hands 256,000 m² of the old Bobadela logistics site to Loures
items.summary: The government is transferring 256,161 m² of the former Bobadela logistics complex — now home to Pope Francis Park — to Loures council.
items.why: A quarter of a million square metres of public land changing hands on the Lisbon riverfront logistics corridor is a long-dated supply signal in a tight industrial market.

items.headline: Luís Mota Duarte to lead Sonae Sierra from January 2027
items.summary: He becomes CEO in January, succeeding Fernando Guedes de Oliveira, who has run the group for more than 15 years.
items.why: A leadership change at one of Iberia's largest retail and mixed-use platforms can reset strategy, disposals and capital partners across the region.

items.headline: Coldwell Banker opens its first Porto agency
items.summary: Marking its 120th year, the brokerage launched a Porto office and absorbed a 10-strong team from Homelovers Porto.
items.why: International brokerages doubling down on Porto confirm the northern market's institutional coming-of-age — more intermediated stock and sharper price discovery.

items.headline: New RJUE planning regime takes effect — what changes for building and buying
items.summary: The overhauled Urban Development Regime (RJUE) came into force on 1 October, cutting bureaucracy across construction, rehabilitation and property sales.
items.why: Licensing speed is the single biggest driver of development returns in Portugal; if the reform delivers, it lifts feasibility on stalled schemes.

items.headline: Rules land for investing in 'moderate rent' housing
items.summary: A regulatory order sets out the requirements for Moderate Rent Investment Contracts (CIA), the framework for investors backing capped-rent homes.
items.why: It creates a defined, incentivised product for institutional residential capital — a potential entry route into Portuguese living with policy tailwinds.

items.headline: Asking prices up 7.9% in September to a new record €3,228/m²
items.summary: September asking prices rose 7.9% year-on-year to a record median, while quarterly growth cooled to +0.5%.
items.why: A fresh record with decelerating quarterly momentum points to a market still rising but losing pace — entry timing matters.

items.headline: Portugal leads the EU for house-price growth
items.summary: Portugal topped the bloc at 16.5% year-on-year in Q2, against a eurozone average of just 1.1%, per Eurostat.
items.why: Being the EU's fastest-rising market pulls in cross-border capital — and sharpens the affordability and regulatory risk funds must underwrite.

readForFund.lead: Pricing power is still the story.
readForFund.text: EU-topping +16.5% growth and a fresh €3,228/m² record argue for underwriting to continued scarcity, not reversion.

readForFund.lead: Deregulation is the catalyst to watch.
readForFund.text: The new RJUE regime could compress licensing timelines — the biggest lever on Portuguese development IRRs.
Euribor near two-year highs trims leveraged buyers but widens the gap institutional equity can exploit.
The new CIA framework formalises an investable moderate-rent product for patient, policy-aligned capital.
